Curator-driven backtest — 2024-05-06 to 2026-05-01

The watchlist-curator agent was called weekly over the 2024-05-06 to 2026-05-01 window. At each rebalance it read a date-clean news pool for the preceding weekly window (built upstream from GDELT GKG + Wayback, look-ahead-reduced) and proposed adds and removes against the active watchlist; the optimizer then ran mean-variance on the revised watchlist. Each rebalance is marked by an orange square on the curator curve in chart 1 — hover over one to see that rebalance's adds, removes, and the curator's rationale. The buy-and-hold curve below is the value of the initial portfolio (which never gets rebalanced or optimized) over time. The buy-and-hold portfolio has equal amounts of [AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, NVDA, SPY] and is held without any rebalancing across the window. Throughout the charts below: general_markets = defensive equity ETFs (broad-market / dividend / utilities / staples); cashlike = bonds + cash-equivalents + precious metals (e.g., AGG, BIL, IAU).

2024-05-04 — no changes · 17 queries

Rationale: This week's pool is dominated by noise that does not clear the bar for a managed-slot swap: dozens of foreign-military missile/loitering-munition test reports (India, China, South Korea, Poland) with no clean US-listed pure-play attached; private-company space news (SpaceX Starship refueling, Blue Origin competitive color) with no ticker; generic robotics-competition PR (FIRST Robotics, Nigerian delegates, BroomBots) with zero commercial content; and a thin, just-uplisted microcap (Serve Robotics/SERV, $40M raise, days-old Nasdaq listing) that fails the liquidity/seasoning bar for a first look. The more credible wave signals -- Cameco (CCJ) catching a bid on the Senate's Russian-uranium-import ban, and Vistra (VST) adding nuclear capacity amid AI-driven power demand -- are genuine nuclear-wave catalysts worth tracking, but neither clearly outperforms the current AI mega-cap slate this week: TSMC beat on AI-chip demand, Meta shipped Llama 3, and Microsoft put $1.5B into G42, all reinforcing that the current AI wave (AAPL/GOOGL/MSFT/NVDA) is still mid-cycle, not cresting, with no thesis-breach evidence against any current holding (the reported AI-stock pullback was broad-market and sentiment-driven, not fundamental). Rocket Lab (RKLB) drew a bearish options print with no offsetting catalyst, and the defense-prime contract flow (Lockheed, Northrop, Raytheon) is real but represents already-mature, mega-cap exposure rather than early-wave entry. With the mandate this week requiring any add to be paired with a remove, and no current holding showing degraded thesis strength, the correct call is no_changes -- watching CCJ/VST for a stronger buildup signal in coming weeks.
